corpus_maintenance: Served frontend assets (status 200, raw-body, text/html|javascript|css) are NOT body-asserted. Their records carry body_assertion instead of body_sha256/body_bytes/body_text, and a record with no body_sha256 is not body-asserted by the replay. Pinning an asset's bytes is not a product assertion -- it reddens on every deliberate frontend edit and says nothing about what changed -- and with no recorder left the only repair was hand-patching a hash. Status, content type, content disposition and Location are still asserted for these routes, and API response bodies (normalized-json) are still fully asserted. Assert frontend CONTENT with a targeted check on the thing you care about, never a whole-file digest.
coverage_limitations: ⛔ Do not quote the mutation-phase CASE COUNT as coverage. Read `mutation_census` below, which is COMPUTED from the recorded cases: it separates probes that actually mutated (2xx on a mutating method) from refusals and post-state reads, and reports how many routes were successfully called TWICE WITH THE SAME INPUT -- the only number that speaks to the fill-only-when-absent class. The replay therefore pins that a first call succeeds and says NOTHING about a second call with the same input. Two helpers under these routes are fill-only-when-absent: think/facets.create_facet raises on collision (six lines above a tolerant mkdir(exist_ok=True)), and think/activities.append_activity_record appends unless the id exists (guard in a nested closure). A port that overwrites, rotates or duplicates on a second call REPLAYS GREEN against this fixture. Assert both directions in unit tests.

Captured with SOLSTONE_DISABLE_CONVEY_SIDE_RUNTIMES=1, so any field a live side runtime populates is pinned in its ABSENT state. These four surfaces are filesystem projections and none reads a side runtime -- checked, not assumed -- but do not widen that claim to a route added later.

The PDF case pins status, content type, disposition and pdf_text. reference_body_sha256 is a RECORD of what weasyprint emitted and must NOT be asserted by a port; no native renderer will reproduce those bytes.

🔴 EVERY GET ROUTE ON THIS SURFACE WRITES, via `think/utils.get_journal`, whose docstring reads 'Return the journal path. Auto-creates the directory.' and which calls os.makedirs on every resolution. It is the deepest and most shared instance of the read-named-writer class in the tree, and a method-keyed AST sweep over GET-only handlers is what found it -- reading did not.

⚠ THIRD FAILURE MODE, on this surface's READ routes: two read-named helpers WRITE. `think/awareness._awareness_dir` and `think/facet_review_candidates.facet_review_candidates_dir` both mkdir on the way to a GET, so `GET /app/awareness/api/state` and `GET /app/curation/api/facet/candidates` are not pure reads. Both docstrings DO disclose it -- 'creating it if needed' -- but after the word 'Return', which is where the eye has already stopped. A replay cannot see a directory that gets created either way.

Routes this lane DELETES are deliberately absent: the activities web UI (/, /{day}, /api/index, /api/stats/{month}, /api/day/{day}/activities, /api/activity_output/{path}) and every /app/reflections/* route. Their absence here is a decision, not an oversight.
generator: RETIRED -- scripts/convey_facets_corpus.py was removed with the Python script surface and no replacement recorder exists, so this fixture is HAND-MAINTAINED. Changing an asset under assets/** goes stale in every raw-body record that pins it, and the corpus replay tests then fail with a digest mismatch. To re-record one: recompute sha256 over the served body (for a static asset that is sha256 of the file itself) and update body_sha256, body_bytes and body_text together, for EVERY record on that path -- body_bytes and body_text are not asserted, so a digest-only fix passes CI while leaving the record self-inconsistent and misleading. Confirm the old recorded digest equals the asset at your change's parent commit before trusting the swap.
